question: Ishan bought some pens at the rate of ₹150/dozen. He sold them for ₹17 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**CP** of 12 pens = 150 ⇒ **CP** of 1 pen = 150 ÷ 12 = 12.5

**SP** of 1 pen = 17

**Profit** = 17 − 12.5 = 4.5

**Profit%** = (4.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100 = 36%

**∴ The correct answer is 36%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Cost Price (CP) = 150 per dozen; Selling Price (SP) = 17 per unit.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c0d58b3970d9c34bbc7458b6a583d5518aa0a36b2f7f63009c86e09f54bdb20.png] 

⇒ **CP** of 12 pens = 150

⇒ **SP** of 12 pens = 17 × 12 = 204

⇒ **Total Profit** = 204 − 150 = 54

⇒ **Profit%** = (54 ÷ 150) × 100 = 36%

**∴ The correct answer is 36%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

Always ensure that the **Cost Price** and **Selling Price** are calculated for the same number of units before finding the profit percentage.

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit% is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise. Formula: [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.</p
